files.lesson.md: --- order: 52 unit: boxplots10 node: AC9M10ST02 n1 uses: [AC9M7ST01 n2, AC9M9ST03 n1] assumes: [AC9M7ST01 n2, AC9M9ST03 n1, AC9M10ST01 n3] connection: median-house-price title: Five numbers summary: "The lowest, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and highest values split a data set into four equal groups and say where the middle half sits." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Property reports quote the middle of the market, not the very top. How do you find it?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8445 url: http://127.0.0.1:8445/index.html readySelector: "#board" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: data.yml#pic, caption: "Eleven sales in order: lowest 480, lower quartile 510, median 560, upper quartile 640, highest 1450 (thousands of dollars)." } --- Property reports give the median price, because a few very high sales drag the mean up ([Westpac explains why](https://www.westpac.com.au/personal-banking/home-loans/median-house-prices-explained/)). A good report also says where the middle half of the sales sit. Eleven houses in one suburb sold last month for these prices, in thousands of dollars, in order: 480, 495, 510, 520, 545, 560, 590, 610, 640, 720 and 1450 (made up for the task). The median is the sixth price, 560. Have a guess where the lower quartile falls, a quarter of the way up, and we'll check at the end of the lesson. ## Predict: a quarter of the way up ```step stage: predict insight: "Choosing the price a quarter of the way up shows who has a feel for splitting the ordered values into four equal groups before any method is taught." check: type: predict q: "The lower quartile has a quarter of the sales at or below it. Which of these prices is the lower quartile of the eleven sales?" options: - "495" - "510" - "520" - "545" actual: "510. It is the middle of the five lowest prices (480, 495, 510, 520, 545), so about a quarter of the sales sit at or below it." ``` ## Run: take away the high sale ```step stage: run insight: "Taking out the one very high sale changes the highest value and hardly moves the median and quartiles, which is why reports quote them." try: { playground: board, starter: "data.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Take 1450 out of the Values box and press Use these values. Which of the five numbers moved a lot, and which hardly moved?", when: "h = 720", explain: "The highest went from 1450 to 720 and the median and quartiles barely moved: the quartiles are 510 and 610, and the median is 552.5. The extreme value stretches the ends but not the middle." } ``` The board draws the sales as dots, with a box from the lower quartile to the upper quartile and a bar at the median. Under it you can read the five numbers. ## Investigate: finding the five numbers ```step stage: investigate insight: "The median splits the ordered values in half and each quartile is the median of one half. When the number of values is odd, the middle value is left out of both halves." tasks: - hint: ["Find the median first. With 9 values it is the 5th.", "Leave the median out when you split into halves."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Nine students' waiting times at the canteen, in minutes and in order, are 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 14, 15 and 20 (made up). What is the interquartile range?" steps: - ["median $= 9$ (the 5th of 9)", "the middle value splits the data in two"] - ["lower half $2, 5, 6, 8$ gives $Q_1 = 5.5$; upper half $11, 14, 15, 20$ gives $Q_3 = 14.5$", "the middle value is left out of both halves"] - ["$14.5 - 5.5 = 9$", "the interquartile range is $Q_3 - Q_1$"] answer: "9" answerLabel: "Interquartile range (minutes)" tolerance: 0.01 feedback: - ["8", "That leaves the median (9) in both halves. With 9 values the middle one is left out of both."] - ["18", "That is the range, 20 − 2. The interquartile range is the length of the middle half."] criteria: - "I found the median first." - "I split the values into two halves." - "I found the median of each half." explain: "Median 9; lower half 2, 5, 6, 8 has median (5 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5.5; upper half 11, 14, 15, 20 has median (14 + 15) ÷ 2 = 14.5. The IQR is 14.5 − 5.5 = 9." - hint: ["Split the eight ordered values into two halves of four.", "The lower half is 4, 6, 9, 11."] check: type: number q: "Eight values in order are 4, 6, 9, 11, 14, 18, 21 and 25. What is the lower quartile?" answer: 7.5 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "Eight values split into two halves of four. The lower half is 4, 6, 9, 11 and its median is (6 + 9) ÷ 2 = 7.5." smaller: check: type: number q: "The lower half of the eight values is 4, 6, 9 and 11. What is its median?" answer: 7.5 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "Four values: the median is halfway between the middle two, (6 + 9) ÷ 2 = 7.5." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#mia" text: "Mia finds the lower quartile of nine waiting times. Click the line where the working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: quartile-halfway-to-extreme explain: "Line 3: the lower quartile is the median of the lower half of the values, not the point halfway between the lowest value and the median. The lower half is 3, 4, 6, 7 and its median is 5." - check: type: question q: "The suburb's five numbers are 480, 510, 560, 640 and 1450 (thousands of dollars). What does the 510 tell you?" options: - "About a quarter of the sales were for $510 000 or less" - "Half of the sales were for $510 000 or less" - "The average sale was $510 000" - "The cheapest sale was $510 000" answer: 0 feedback: - null - "That is the median, 560." - "That would be the mean, and the mean here is about 647." - "The cheapest is the lowest value, 480." explain: "The lower quartile has a quarter of the data at or below it, and the upper quartile has a quarter above it. Between them lies the middle half." ``` ### Five numbers ```worked 3, 4, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 21 :: Ten waiting times in order (made up). \text{lowest } 3,\ \text{highest } 21 :: The two ends. \tfrac{7 + 9}{2} = 8 :: Ten values: the median is halfway between the 5th and 6th. Q_1 = 4 :: The lower half is 3, 4, 4, 6, 7. Its median is 4. Q_3 = 12 :: The upper half is 9, 10, 12, 13, 21. Its median is 12. 12 - 4 = 8 :: The interquartile range is the length of the middle half. ``` Now try one on paper: nine waiting times in order, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 14, 15 and 20. With nine values the median is the fifth one, and it is left out when you split into halves. ### Lower quartile ### Find the mistake ### What a quartile says ## Modify: change the data ```step stage: modify insight: "Changing the data shows which of the five numbers an extreme value moves and how an even count changes the quartiles." try: { playground: board, starter: "data.yml#modify", height: 600 } tasks: - check: type: question q: "Change 1450 to 2400 in the Values box and press Use these values. Which of the five numbers change?" options: - "Only the highest" - "The highest and the upper quartile" - "All five" - "None of them" answer: 0 feedback: - null - "The upper quartile is the median of the upper half, which is 590, 610, 640, 720, 2400, and that is still 640." - "The middle values don't move when only the highest moves." - "The highest value is one of the five numbers, and it changed." explain: "The highest value changes. The median and quartiles stay at 560, 510 and 640, because the order of the other values hasn't changed." - hint: ["With 12 values the median is halfway between the 6th and 7th.", "Put 600 between 590 and 610 in the order."] check: type: number q: "Edge case: a twelfth sale of 600 is added to the original eleven (1450 back in). What is the median now? (thousands of dollars)" answer: 575 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "Twelve values: the median is halfway between the 6th (560) and the 7th (590): (560 + 590) ÷ 2 = 575. The lower quartile is 515 and the upper quartile is 625." - hint: ["Four values split into two halves of two.", "Each half's median is halfway between its two values."] check: type: number q: "Only four sales are left: 480, 510, 640 and 720. What is the lower quartile? (thousands of dollars)" answer: 495 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "The lower half is 480 and 510, and its median is (480 + 510) ÷ 2 = 495. The upper quartile is (640 + 720) ÷ 2 = 680." ``` ### An even higher sale ### An even number of values ### Only four values ## Practise: quartiles and the spread of the middle half ```step stage: practise insight: "Finding quartiles and the interquartile range from ordered values, with a review of the mean." tasks: - hint: ["Seven values: the median is the 4th, and the halves are the first three and last three.", "The upper half is the 5th, 6th and 7th values."] check: { type: number, q: "Seven values in order are 3, 6, 7, 10, 12, 15 and 18. What is the upper quartile?", answer: 15, tolerance: 0.01, explain: "The median is 10 (the 4th). The upper half is 12, 15, 18 and its median is 15." } - hint: ["Quartile 3 take away quartile 1.", "Median of each half first."] check: { type: number, q: "Eight values in order are 2, 5, 7, 9, 12, 14, 20 and 26. What is the interquartile range?", answer: 11, tolerance: 0.01, explain: "Lower half 2, 5, 7, 9 has median 6. Upper half 12, 14, 20, 26 has median 17. The IQR is 17 − 6 = 11." } - hint: ["Add all eleven prices, then divide by 11.", "The prices add to 7120."] check: { type: number, q: "Review: what is the mean of the eleven sale prices (480, 495, 510, 520, 545, 560, 590, 610, 640, 720, 1450)? (nearest thousand dollars)", answer: 647, tolerance: 0.6, explain: "The prices add to 7120 and 7120 ÷ 11 is about 647. That is higher than the upper quartile, 640, because the one very high sale drags the mean up." } ``` ### Upper quartile ### Interquartile range ### Review ## Make: the middle half of the market ```step stage: make insight: "Back to the suburb: how wide is the range where the middle half of the sales sit, and why quote it instead of the highest and lowest." tasks: - hint: ["Median of the lower five, median of the upper five.", "640 − 510."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "The report says the middle half of last month's sales were spread over a range of how many thousand dollars? Use the eleven prices." steps: - ["median $= 560$ (the 6th of 11)", "the middle price is left out of both halves"] - ["lower half $480, 495, 510, 520, 545$ gives $Q_1 = 510$; upper half $590, 610, 640, 720, 1450$ gives $Q_3 = 640$", "the median of each half of five"] - ["$640 - 510 = 130$", "the interquartile range"] answer: "130" answerLabel: "Width of the middle half (thousands of dollars)" tolerance: 0.01 feedback: - ["970", "That is the whole range, 1450 − 480. The one very high sale stretches it, and it says nothing about the middle."] - ["80", "That is the upper quartile take away the median (640 − 560). The middle half runs from the lower quartile to the upper quartile."] criteria: - "I found the lower and upper quartiles." - "I took the lower quartile from the upper quartile." - "I could say why this beats the whole range." explain: "The quartiles are 510 and 640, so the middle half of the sales spread over 640 − 510 = 130, about $130 000. The whole range, 970, is stretched by the one very high sale." - check: type: question q: "Why does the report quote the quartiles rather than the lowest and highest prices?" options: - "The quartiles describe where most sales are, and one very high sale doesn't stretch them" - "The lowest and highest prices are always wrong" - "Quartiles are bigger numbers" - "The highest price doesn't count as a sale" answer: 0 feedback: - null - "They are real sales, they just tell you about the extremes." - "Quartiles aren't bigger, they are in the middle." - "It is a real sale. It just isn't typical." explain: "The highest and lowest are single sales at the extremes. The quartiles show where the typical sales sit." ``` ### The middle half Work this out on paper first, then type your answer. ### Why the quartiles The suburb and its sales are made up for the task. **Also used in** - **Waiting times and wages.** Reports of waiting times, incomes and house prices quote the median and quartiles for the same reason. - **Exams.** A school might report the lower quartile, the median and the upper quartile of a test's marks. - **Next lesson.** Boxplots: drawing the five numbers as one picture. ```teacher summary: Students find the five-number summary (lowest, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, highest) by the median-of-halves method, say what each number means, and see why reports quote the middle half rather than the extremes (AC9M10ST02, node 1). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 9 min · Investigate 14 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can find the five numbers of a data set. - I can say what each of the five numbers tells you. - I can find the interquartile range. struggle: "Where to split: whether the median is in a half, and what to do with an even count. Ask: how many values are in each half, and is the middle one left out?" before: > Students need the median (Year 7) and a feel for skewed data and outliers (Year 9). The ethics of data (AC9M10ST01 node 3) isn't a lesson here; it is taught in class, as the previous two lessons lead into it. This is a hinge lesson: a wrong quartile gives a wrongly drawn boxplot in the next lesson, so check every student can find the median of a half before moving on. The method here is the median of each half. With an odd number of values the middle value is left out of both halves; with an even number it is not a value at all, so nothing is left out. Different books use different conventions, and a spreadsheet's quartile function can give slightly different answers (it may interpolate), so tell students the rule this site uses before they check a result against a calculator or spreadsheet. The Year 10 curriculum's wider tier asks students to compare conventions; that is a good extension here. The suburb's sales, the canteen waiting times and the test values are made up for the task. The Westpac page is for the idea that reports use medians for house prices because a few very high or low prices skew the average. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the check. Don't reveal the method; the Investigate does that." - "Run: ask which numbers the highest sale changed before anyone presses the button." - "Paper: the nine-value try-one and the Make are worked on paper first. Walk the room and check each student finds the median first." - "Modify: the even count (twelve values) is the edge case." stuck: - see: A student gives the lower quartile as halfway between the lowest value and the median. ask: Is the lower quartile a distance, or the middle value of a group? fix: "It is the median of the lower half of the ordered values: a value (or a halfway point between two values) from the data, not a point halfway along a line." - see: A student leaves the median in both halves for an odd count and gets 8 not 9. ask: How many values are in each half? Is any value counted twice? fix: With nine values, take the 5th out as the median; the halves are the first four and the last four. - see: A student says the interquartile range is the highest minus the lowest. ask: Which values does the box (the middle half) go between? fix: That is the range. The interquartile range is the upper quartile take away the lower quartile. stretch: Compare this method with a spreadsheet's quartile function on the eleven prices. Do they agree? Why might they not? support: Write the values on strips of paper, fold the ordered strip in half, then fold each half again. The folds are the quartiles. leads: > Continues AC9M10ST02 (node 1; a hinge). Where it leads: boxplots (next), which draw the five numbers as one picture, and then comparing distributions. exit: q: Seven values in order are 4, 7, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 22. What are the lower and upper quartiles? a: Median 12. Lower half 4, 7, 9 gives 7. Upper half 15, 18, 22 gives 18. explain: > The five numbers are the lowest value, the lower quartile, the median, the upper quartile and the highest value. They cut the ordered data into four groups of about the same size. Find the median, then the median of each half; when there is an odd number of values the middle one is left out of both halves. The interquartile range, upper quartile take away lower quartile, is the length of the middle half. sources: - title: "Median house prices explained (Westpac): medians are used for house prices because a few unusually high or low prices can skew the average" url: https://www.westpac.com.au/personal-banking/home-loans/median-house-prices-explained/ checked: 2026-10-22 ```

# Mia's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: mia
The nine times in order are 3, 4, 6, 7, 12, 13, 15, 16, 20, and the median is the fifth one, 12.
The lowest time is 3.
The lower quartile is halfway between the lowest time and the median.
(3 + 12) ÷ 2 = 7.5, so the lower quartile is 7.5.
# endregion
